headline: [[q|Israel began committing genocide.]] Two of the most-read opening sections now say it in Wikipedia’s own voice.
unit: sentences charging Israel with genocide, plus Israel’s denial: Jan 2021, Jul 2023, now (5 Nov 2026), in the opening sections of the 150 most-read articles that already existed in January 2021
body: The two in Wikipedia’s own voice are the articles on Israel and on Benjamin Netanyahu. In the Israel article the next sentence is [[q|Israel has denied that its actions constitute genocide.]] The Netanyahu article carries no denial. Five others attribute the charge. In these 150 articles no sentence charges Hamas or Palestinians with genocide. Newer articles are not in this count: the October 7 attacks article, created in 2023, says [[q|Some have alleged that the attack was an act of genocide or a genocidal massacre against Israelis.]]

headline: “Militant” left Hamas’s definition. Hamas is now [[q|a Sunni Islamist Palestinian nationalist political organisation with a military wing]].
unit: 19:12 UTC, in the Hamas article’s most-read month (8,236,474 views); timing only
body: “Terrorist” was written into the definition five times; none lasted a day. The designation sentence moved from sentence 5 of 20 (2021) to 22 of 23 (Oct 2026). Neither the Hamas nor the Israel opening section mentions the hostages.

headline: 1948 got an agent. The Nakba is now [[q|the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists]], in Wikipedia’s own voice.
unit: 1948 articles quoted in this report now name the agent in their opening section (Nakba, 1948 Palestine war, 1948 Arab–Israeli War); the fourth, 1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight, removed it from its first sentence
body: The 1948 Palestine war went from [[q|around 700,000 Palestinian Arabs were displaced]] (2023) to [[q|Zionist forces conquered about 78% of the former territory of the mandate, causing the expulsion and flight of over 700,000 Palestinians]]. The exodus of Jews from Arab states is still written with no agent: [[q|Hundreds of thousands of Jews fled or were expelled from Arab states]].

headline: Occupation is more often stated in Wikipedia’s own voice, for Israel and for Russia alike.
unit: occupation charges against Israel in Wikipedia’s own voice: 16 of 35 (2021), 44 of 55 (now), in the 150 most-read opening sections
body: Many of the new ones are history (the 1967 war, Suez) and events of 2024 to 2026. The legal-status sentences that changed are in the West Bank and Israel opening sections: [[q|Since 1967, the territory has been under Israeli occupation, which is illegal under international law.]] Occupation charged to Russia in Crimea and to Turkey in northern Cyprus went from 25% to 74% own voice. Since the July 2024 ICJ advisory opinion, editors have a court to cite. The share of harm sentences naming Israel as the one doing harm barely moved: 23.6% to 26.4%, not statistically clear.

headline: Off-wiki canvassing is documented on both sides. The surge began before the Discord channel.
unit: topic insertions of critical terms against comparison, in the 16 weeks after 7 Oct 2023; 2.0× while the channel was active
body: Wikipedia’s arbitration committee found pro-Israel email canvassing (January 2024 motions; dating from about October 2023, inside the same 16 weeks) and sanctioned editors for acting on off-wiki canvassing from a pro-Palestinian Discord channel (December 2024), with two more site bans for separate off-wiki coordination (April 2025).[[verify|ArbCom items read from search snippets only; check primary pages (ORGS.md section 5)]] The period ratios follow the war’s tempo; they cannot show whether the channel added to the editing. In our data, two small groups of four long-standing accounts moved together on the same articles beyond chance (14 linked pairs, where chance gives about 2). None edited in step, no wording was pasted across articles, and their timing matches neither documented window clearly. Our footprint tests could only have seen very large effects.

headline: The core moved; the long tail did not. The more central the article, the more its opening paragraph changed.
unit: of the Top-importance Israel, Palestine and Jewish-topic articles gained critical vocabulary in their opening paragraph since July 2023 (121 Top articles sampled); other conflict regions 4.4%. Gap +5.9 points, range +0.9 to +11.2
body: Mid importance: 1.5% against none of the 362 comparison articles sampled. Low-importance and ungraded pages, about 80% of the 49,000 topic articles, moved no more than elsewhere; across all of them the gap is 0.4 points, within the margin of error. Articles on Judaism did not move. The wave ran through 2024, about 16 new critical terms per 1,000 edits against about 7 before the war, and was back to 5 to 6 by 2026.
